title: The Limit Is in the Input, Not the Model: State-Dependent Command Safety in Natural-Language Interfaces to Industrial Controllers
abstract: arXiv:2611.24682v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Language models judging commands to industrial controllers may not receive machine state, the equipment's current condition. The same command can require opposite safety decisions in different states, so an incorrect answer may reflect missing information rather than poor reasoning. We propose an answerability audit: does the model receive the information needed to decide? The audit records the model's inputs and pairs the same command with two states requiring opposite answers. The paired score counts a pair only when both answers are correct. We add rules, then state values, to the model's input. In an author-built test of 15 pairs from three systems with four language models, none reliably distinguished the paired cases without state, even with rules. With state, scores ranged from 0 to 13 correct pairs out of 15; three models improved. With text alone, one model always allowed commands and another always denied them. Their overall

translated_title: 局限在于输入而非模型：工业控制器自然语言接口中的状态依赖命令安全性
translated_abstract: 语言模型在判断发送给工业控制器的命令时，可能没有接收到机器状态，即设备当前的状况。同一条命令在不同的状态下可能需要截然相反的安全决策，因此错误的回答可能反映的是信息缺失而非推理能力不足。我们提出了一种“可判定性审计”：即模型是否收到了做出决策所需的信息？该审计记录模型的输入，并将同一条命令与两个需要相反答案的状态配对。只有当两个答案都正确时，配对分数才被计入。我们先向模型输入中添加规则，再添加状态值。在一项由作者构建的、来自三个系统的15对测试用例、使用四个语言模型的测试中，在没有状态信息的情况下，即使提供了规则，没有任何模型能够可靠地区分这些配对用例。提供状态后，得分范围从15对中正确0对到13对不等；其中三个模型有所改进。仅依靠文本时，一个模型总是允许命令执行，另一个模型总是拒绝命令。它们的总体
tldr: 本文提出“可判定性审计”方法，证明语言模型在判断工业控制器命令安全性时的失误源于输入中缺失机器状态信息而非模型推理能力不足，且提供状态值可显著提升判断的准确性。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an answerability audit demonstrating that language models' failures in judging industrial controller command safety stem from missing machine-state information in the input rather than poor reasoning, and that supplying state values substantially improves their safety decisions.
